projects.name: Neural scene representation
projects.description: Using DNNs to generate 3D environments from small sets of images
projects.long_description: Deep neural networks are used to generate 3D environments from a small set of images. The input to the model is a *context* and a *query* pose, where the *context* is a small set of images annotated with the camera poses. The model then renders the image from the *query* pose. The training code is written in both TensorFlow 2 and PyTorch. The research is conducted on CIIRC, CTU with Erik Derner and prof. Robert Babuška.

projects.name: Deep RL PyTorch
projects.long_description: The project is a library of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms written for PyTorch. Some of the implemented algorithms are PAAC, A3C, PPO, DQN, and Rainbow. The library is primarily used in other projects.

projects.name: LemmaTag
projects.description: Implementation of SoTA lemmatizer and tagger achieving 98.75% and 96.67% accuracies respectively on UD Treebank
projects.long_description: This project is an implementation of SoTA lemmatizer and tagger achieving 98.75% and 96.67% accuracies respectively on UD Treebank. The source code was written for TensorFlow 2. Pre-trained models are available for the Czech language.

projects.name: DMHouse
projects.description: An indoor 3D environment simulator for pre-training VN agents
projects.long_description: The DMHouse project is a fork of the DMLab 3D environment published by DeepMind. In the simulator, there are new environments implemented which resemble office rooms. There is also a Python gym interface allowing the simulator to be used directly by DRL algorithms.

projects.name: AuGPT task-oriented dialogue system
projects.description: A task-oriented dialogue system implemented for DSTC9 competition
projects.long_description: AuGPT is a task-oriented dialogue system based on the SOLOIST architecture. It uses massive data augmentation by paraphrasing the original dataset using back-translations. The code was written for PyTorch. The paper was accepted to NLP4ConvAI, EMNLP 2021. The project was developed in collaboration with the dialogue group from UFAL, Charles University, and our team participated in the DSTC9 competition.

projects.name: Real-world visual navigation using DRL
projects.description: Applying DRL visual navigation method to real-world mobile robot.
projects.long_description: In this project, a prior deep reinforcement learning visual navigation method was modified to be applied directly to a real-world mobile robot. The method was evaluated in a real office room. The paper was published in the RA-L journal (IF = 3.6) and accepted to ICRA 2021. The research was conducted on CIIRC, CTU with Erik Derner and prof. Robert Babuška.

projects.name: Visual navigation using DRL
projects.description: Implementing a visual navigation method using a PAAC-based algorithm with auxiliary tasks.
projects.long_description: The goal of this project was to design a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agent able to navigate in a simulated environment using an RGB camera only where navigation goal is also given as an RGB image. A new method called A2CAT-VN was proposed, which was based on the PAAC algorithm. It used auxiliary tasks which improved the convergence properties. The research was conducted on CIIRC, CTU with Erik Derner and prof. Robert Babuška.

projects.name: Object detection on KITTI-360
projects.long_description: This project focused on the object detection used in autonomous cars. State-of-the-art (at that time) methods were reimplemented, including RetinaNet and Mask R-CNN. Effective training pipelines were developed to efficiently train the object detection model. The code was written in TensorFlow 1 but, unfortunately, is not publicly available.
projects.description: Designing new object detection approaches based on RetinaNet and Mask R-CNN

courses.mini_description: zero-sum games, MCTS, A*, CSP, MDP, EA, planning, knowledge representation

courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the symbolic artificial intelligence. It presents the algorithms for informed and non-informed state space search, nontraditional methods of problem solving, knowledge representation by means of formal logic, methods of automated reasoning and introduction to markovian decision making.
